cards.b: Energy from sources replaced naturally that will not run out, e.g. wind, solar.
Sources that will run out, e.g. coal, oil, gas and nuclear.
The proportion of each energy source a country uses.
Floods land and homes, high cost, damages river ecosystems.
Release CO₂, cause pollution and will run out.
Large output with no CO₂ in use, but radioactive waste and accident risk.
Water stored in underground rocks (aquifers) reached by wells.
Physical: not enough water. Economic: water exists but cannot be supplied for lack of money.
Rising demand, pollution, drought, leaks, overuse of groundwater and poor management.
Removing salt from sea water; very costly and energy hungry.
Natural heat-trapping versus extra warming caused by human emissions of CO₂ and methane.
Sea level rise, melting ice, extreme weather, changing rainfall, species loss.

gaps.s: Energy sources that run out are called ___.
Electricity from flowing water is ___ power.
Removing salt from sea water is called ___.
Water stored underground in rocks is ___.
The biggest user of water worldwide is ___.
Fertiliser run-off causing algae blooms is called ___.
Gases such as CO₂ and methane are ___ gases.
Development that does not harm the future is called ___ development.

short.q: Explain why energy demand is rising worldwide.
short.model: Population is growing, and so is industry in NICs. Higher living standards mean more people own appliances and vehicles.

short.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of HEP.
short.model: HEP is reliable and releases no CO₂ when generating. However, building a dam floods land and homes and affects ecosystems.

short.q: Explain how water pollution can lead to a water shortage.
short.model: Pollution makes supplies unsafe to drink or use. Treatment is costly, so less usable water is available and shortages result.

short.q: Describe two effects of sea level rise.
short.model: Low-lying coasts and islands are flooded, and farmland is made salty. Homes are lost and people migrate.

short.q: Explain how industry can damage the environment.
short.model: Factories burn fossil fuels that release CO₂ and cause air pollution. Waste can be dumped in rivers, harming wildlife.
